chronic arsenic poisoning causes skin cancer in humans, and that the prevalence of arsenic skin cancer increases with age and with duration and level of arsenic exposure.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevalence of arsenic-related skin cancer and the risk factors of skin cancer among 468 men and of 613 women aged 30 or above in 14 villages in Taiwan.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

chronic arseniasis in Taiwanese villages is a multifactorial disease, in that the prevalence of skin cancer is associated not only with chronic exposure to high-arsenic water but also with chronic liver dysfunction, malnutrition and aging.
the evidence is inadequate to determine the carcinogenicity of inorganic arsenicals in humans.
the risk factors for skin cancer in the Taiwanese population are: (1) chronic arsenic exposure; (2) hepatitis B virus infection with liver dysfunction; and (3) undernourishment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic exposure to inorganic arsenic, particularly at a young age, can lead to the development of skin cancer in a dose-response fashion.
the risk of skin cancer in arseniasis endemic areas is related to the duration of arsenic intake, the cumulative amount of arsenic intake and the presence of liver dysfunction.
arseniasis is a multifactorial disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel mechanism for how arsenic can induce skin cancer in humans.
the skin is an important organ for the development of arsenic-induced cancers, especially skin cancer, and that arsenic-induced skin cancers are not rare.
the risk factors for arsenic-induced skin cancers are the same as for arsenicosis in general.
